_description: Design point of the 1F1C target with 64 x 64 arrays: the default design point (Laleni et al., 'A High-Efficiency Charge-Domain CIM 1F1C Macro Using 2-bit FeFET Cells for DNN Processing', IEEE JXCDC 2024; ../default/design.json) with the array size, the ADC resolution and ISAAC's weight-flip encoding changed (Shafiee et al., ISCA 2016, paper/devices/isaac_shafiee2016.pdf). Every value has its source in _provenance. 'reported_results' are Laleni's outputs at 128 x 128, kept only to check our simulations against, never used as inputs.

adc.type: SAR, single-ended, conventional switching, bootstrapped sampling switch, input buffer

_provenance.architecture: Laleni Sec. III: each cell is one FeFET (RMU) with its own CMoM (WMU); the FeFET loads into the CMoM of the same cell, so RMU and WMU are coupled per cell
_provenance.process.node_nm: Laleni Sec. V: 'designed and simulated in 28-nm process technology'; FeFETs fabricated in 28 nm HKMG (Sec. III-A, Fig. 5)
_provenance.process.vdd_V: Laleni Sec. V: 'The supply voltage is chosen as VDD = 1 V'
_provenance.array.rows, array.cols: Our design point (array-size sweep: 64, 128). cols are the data columns the mapper uses; the unit column (encoding) is extra
_provenance.encoding: ISAAC Sec. III, 'Encoding to Reduce ADC Size': a column whose weights are collectively large is stored flipped (W' = 2^w - 1 - W), which guarantees the MSB of its sum of products is 0 and lowers the ADC resolution by one bit; a flipped column's result is (2^w - 1) * sum(a_i) - its sum, with sum(a_i) from one extra 'unit column' per array, and one bit per column records whether it is flipped. unit_cell_level: our decision, the unit column's cells store level 1, so its sum is sum(a_i) (at most rows, within the ADC range); the shift-and-add multiplies it by 2^w - 1
_provenance.cell: Laleni, as ../default/design.json (bits_per_cell: Title, Sec. III-C; W/L: Sec. III-A; CMoM: Sec. IV, V; Vth states: Sec. V, Fig. 10)
_provenance.clock.freq_MHz: Laleni Sec. V: 'The sampling frequency (Fs) of the operation is 20 MHz'
_provenance.clock.column_phase_cycles: As ../default/design.json (Laleni Sec. III-B, Fig. 4; reset and accumulate one cycle each, our assumption)
_provenance.adc.type: Laleni Sec. IV, V: conventional single-ended SAR ADC with a bootstrap sampling switch and an input buffer
_provenance.adc.bits: ISAAC Eq. 2 (v = 1 input bit per cycle, w = 2 bits per cell, so A = log2(R) + v + w - 1 = log2(64) + 2 = 8), minus the one bit of ISAAC's weight-flip encoding: 7
_provenance.adc.cycles_per_conversion: Laleni Sec. V: 'eight cycles are needed to quantize the result' by the 7-bit ADC: one sampling cycle and one cycle per bit, so bits + 1 = 8
_provenance.adc.vrefp_V, adc.vrefn_V: Laleni Sec. V: 'Vrefp = 0.5 V and Vrefn = 0 V'; kept at every resolution (the LSB is Vrefp / 2^bits)
_provenance.adc.buffer_bias_uA: The default's 7-bit ADC unchanged (spice/adc/sar_full_tb.sp, same front end), so its bias: ../default/design.json (spice/adc/run_full.py bias sweep)
_provenance.write: Laleni Sec. III-C: write-verify; HVT reset with -5 V for 500 ns, then 1.4 V pulses for 200 ns, increased in 40 mV steps with read-verify until the target Vth
_provenance.reported_results.cpar_fF: Laleni Sec. IV/V: 'Cpar = 75 fF' for 128 rows (our NVSim cell height is fitted to it, see ../default/1f1c.cell)
_provenance.reported_results.kappa: Laleni Sec. V: 'the input range drops to 69%'
_provenance.reported_results.adc_enob_bits, adc_wald: Laleni Sec. V: 'ENOB ... 6.4 bits', 'Walden FoM of the ADC is 26 fJ/conversion'
_provenance.reported_results.bl_charging_power_nW: Laleni Sec. V: 'BL charging power is 0.86 nW with the expected value of weight as (VDD/2)'
_provenance.reported_results.cifar10_vgg8_accuracy_p: Laleni Sec. V: VGG-8 on CIFAR-10 with NeuroSim, 89%
